title: Notation
body_md: We denote the unit circle as $\mathbb{S}^1$, a point of which is a phase. The $n$-dimensional torus is denoted by $\mathbb{T}^n = \mathbb{S}\times\dots\times\mathbb{S}$. Given a set $\mathcal{S}$, $|\mathcal{S}|$ stands for its cardinality. For two sets $\mathcal{S}_1$ and $\mathcal{S}_2$, $\mathcal{S}_1\backslash\mathcal{S}_2$ is their set-theoretic difference. Given $A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times m}$, $B:=[A]^+$ is the matrix where $b_{ij}=a_{ij}$ if $a_{ij}>0$ and $b_{ij}=0$ otherwise. Given matrices $A_1,\dots,A_r$, ${\rm blkdiag}(A_1,\dots,A_r)$ is the block-diagonal matrix of them.

body_md:
\label{invariance}
 For $k=1,2,\dots, r$:  i) the natural frequencies satisfy $\omega_i=\omega_j$ for any $i,j \in \mathcal{C}_k$; and ii) the coupling strengths satisfy that, for any $\ell\in\{1,2,\dots,r\}\backslash\{k\}$,  $\sum_{p\in \mathcal{C}_\ell}(a_{ip}-a_{jp})=0$ for any $i,j \in \mathcal{C}_k$. \null \hfill\ensuremath{\triangle}

title: Lemma
body_md: Let $\lambda^{-1}_{\max}(\bar X_k)$ and $\lambda^{-1}_{\max}( X_k)$ be the solutions to the equations \eqref{Ly:controlled} and \eqref{Ly:uncontrolled}, respectively. There exists a vibrational control input such that $\lambda^{-1}_{\max}(\bar X_k)> \lambda^{-1}_{\max}(X_k)$ \emph{only if} $\mathcal{G}_k$ is not a uniformly weighted complete graph\footnote{A uniformly weighted complete graph is a complete graph in which every edge has the same weight.}.

title: Lemma
body_md:
Assume that the vibrational control is such that $P(t)$  in the system~\eqref{expres:JandP}  satisfies \eqref{P(t)}. Then, the state transition matrix $\Phi(t,t_0)={\rm blkdiag}(\Phi_1,\dots,\Phi_r)$ satisfies
	\begin{align*}
		\scalebox{0.9}{\mbox{\ensuremath{\displaystyle \Phi_k=\begin{bmatrix}
				1 &0 &0 &\cdots &0 &0\\
				\Phi_{21}^{(k)} &1 &0& \cdots &0 &0\\
				\Phi_{31}^{(k)} &\Phi_{32}^{(k)} &1 &\cdots &0 &0\\
				\vdots&\vdots &\vdots&\ddots&\vdots&\vdots\\
				\Phi_{\bar n_k,1}^{(k)} &\Phi_{\bar n_k,2}^{(k)} &\Phi_{\bar n_k,3}^{(k)} &\cdots &\Phi_{\bar n_k,\bar n_k-1}^{(k)} &1			
		\end{bmatrix}}}},
	\end{align*}
where $\scalebox{1}{\mbox{\ensuremath{\displaystyle \Phi_{ij}^{(k)}(t)=-u_{ij}^{(k)}(\cos (t)-\cos(t_0))}}}$.

title: Proof
body_md:
We construct the proof by considering a specific configuration of vibrational control. 
	
	Without loss of generality, we assume that each $B_{{\rm intra}}^{(k)}$ and $\hat B_{{\rm intra}}^{(k)}$ are ordered in a way such that their first $\bar n_k=n_k-1$ columns are the same, and the first two column are $e_2-e_1$ and $e_3-e_2$, respectively, where $e_i$ is the $i$th column of $I_{ n_k}$. Then, there exists a matrix $\tilde{R}^{(k)}_1$ such that 
	$
		R_1^{(k)}={\begin{bmatrix}
				I_{\bar n_k}\\ \tilde{R}^{(k)}_1
		\end{bmatrix}}.
	$

Let $U^{(k)}_{1}(t)=u e_1e_1^\top \sin(t)$ and $U^{(k)}_{2}(t)=-u e_1e_1^\top\sin(t)$.  It can be calculated that 
\begin{align*}
	&P^{(k)}(t)\\
	&= -(\hat B^{(k)}_{{\rm intra}})^\top [B^{(k)}_{{\rm intra}}]^+  U^{(k)}_{1}(t)-[-B^{(k)}_{{\rm intra}}]^{+} U^{(k)}_{2}(t) R_1^{(k)} \\
	&\scalebox{1}{\mbox{\ensuremath{\displaystyle =-(\hat B^{(k)}_{{\rm intra}})^\top u(e_1+e_2)e_1^\top \begin{bmatrix}
			I_{\bar n_k}\\ \tilde{R}^{(k)}_1\end{bmatrix}\sin(t)}}}\\
	&\scalebox{1}{\mbox{\ensuremath{\displaystyle =-u(\hat B^{(k)}_{{\rm intra}})^\top (e_1+e_2) (e_1')^\top\sin(t)   }}},	
\end{align*}
where the second equality follows from $e_1^\top \scalebox{0.7}{\mbox{\ensuremath{\displaystyle \begin{bmatrix}
		I_{\bar n_k}\\ \tilde{R}^{(k)}_1
\end{bmatrix}}}}=(e_1')^\top $ with $e_1'$ being the first column of $I_{\bar n_k}$. Then, it can be seen that the first two rows of $P^{(k)}(t)$ are 
$
	-u(e_2-e_1)^\top (e_1+e_2) (e_1')^\top \sin(t)=0,
$
and 
$
	-u(e_3-e_2)^\top (e_1+e_2) (e_1')^\top=(e'_1)^\top \sin(t),
$
respectively.  The rest rows of $P^{(k)}(t)$ can only have non-zero values at the first column. Therefore, $P^{(k)}(t)$ have the strictly  lower triangular form and satisfies $P^{(k)}(t)\neq 0$, which completes the proof.
